divergences.text: ÉRRORS WERE MADE AT THE TOP
divergences.reason: \b is Unicode in Python: 'É' is a word character there, so no boundary sits before 'RRORS' and the caps run starts at 'WERE'. JS and Go treat 'É' as a non-word character.
Case-insensitive matching folds U+017F LONG S to 's' in Python and Go, so 'It ſeems' matches the term 'it seems'; JS folds only within ASCII.

divergences.text: This is Kind of a problem.
divergences.reason: Python folds U+212A KELVIN SIGN to 'k' and counts it as a word character, so 'kind of' matches. JS folds nothing outside ASCII; Go folds the letter, but its ASCII \b refuses the boundary before it.
U+000B VERTICAL TAB is ASCII, yet the engines part on it: JS's and Python's \s include it, Go's RE2 \s ([\t\n\f\r ]) does not.
